newsitem.title: UK: Mideast tankers steady, Med activity rises fast.
newsitem.headline: Mideast tankers steady, Med activity rises fast.

text.p: Crude tanker fixing in the focal Middle East Gulf remained good and rates were seen steady, ship brokers said on Tuesday.

Chartering did not appear adversely affected by a holiday in Japan. By mid afternoon, one VLCC and ULCC had been seen fixed out of the region. Exxon fixed a 510,000 tonne cargo on the Kapetan Michalis, travelling Middle East Gulf to the Red Sea, with Shell taking a VLCC to the Far East.
"After thinning of tonnage last week, there is an optimism that rates will strengthen over the forthcoming couple of months," a London broker said.
Rates for VLCCs were generally steady, with vessels making trips to Japan, unchanged at W56. Vessels heading to the West could command W52.5, with rates for Eastern voyages around W50.

There was an abundance of activity in the Med/Black Sea sector with no less than five Aframaxes and seven Suezmaxes finding employment. But, this heavy increase in chartering did not herald a rise in rates. Brokers said that 80,000 tonners going cross-Med would have to settle at W97.5.
Suezmaxes were significantly more popular with rates ranged between W70-80 for UKC, Med destinations.
The inter UKC sector retained the buoyancy seen on Monday, with at least five Aframaxes fixed on cross-UK continent trips.
Rates rose further to around W105, up W5 points from last done levels. But, brokers noted that as high as W110 and as low as W92.5 had been done.
Shell UK's chartering of the Stena Concertina, travelling from Sullom Voe at W106.25 was seen to be nearest to typifying the market.
"I can honestly see rates gently increasing further, due to a lessening in tonnage and a large pick up in enquiry," said a Scandinavian broker.
The Caribbean upcoast U.S market saw rates rise marginally to W142.5, up W2.5 points, in a response to a slight decrease in vessel availability in the vicinity.
West African activity was good, with rates on Suezmaxes picking up to W85, up W2.5 points. VLCCs to the U.S were unchanged around W62.5.
